title: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)

sections.label: Volunteering rates rise
sections.summary: About one in five people volunteered in 2014, up from one in 10 in 2000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: About one in five people volunteered in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This is up from one in 10 in the year 2000.

sections.label: Volunteering by age group
sections.summary: In 2016, 29% of respondents aged 25 to 34 volunteered for a social cause, compared with 48% of those aged 35 to 44.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For example, although volunteerism is on the rise, only 29% of respondents aged 25 to 34 volunteered for a social cause in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This compares with 48% of those aged 35 to 44.

sections.label: SG Cares caring society
sections.summary: SG Cares strives to build a caring society where little acts of kindness make Singapore more caring and inclusive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, SG Cares strives to build a caring society where every one of us with little acts of kindness contribute to making Singapore more caring and inclusive.

sections.label: SG Cares and volunteerism
sections.summary: A Member asks how SG Cares has reignited caring, says volunteerism must become part of life, and notes SG Cares launched in November two years back.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In today's busy lifestyle, can the Minister share how SG Cares has helped reignite the support and the spirit of caring in our community to build and strengthen a strong social fabric that will be essential for Singapore and Singaporeans to thrive?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I know that there is a lot of focus on volunteerism in SG Cares and, while I am an advocate for volunteerism, we need to go beyond that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It has got to become part of life and not something that we make time for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I think that is where MSF plays a very critical role in creating that platform for making this happen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the SG Cares movement was launched in Singapore in November two years back to bring together individuals, organisations and beneficiaries.

sections.label: Budget plans for SG Cares
sections.summary: In this year's Budget, the Finance Minister mentioned there will be further plans for SG Cares.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In this year's Budget, the Finance Minister mentioned that there will be further plans for SG Cares.

sections.label: Engaging corporations for philanthropy
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister to share the progress in engaging corporations for philanthropic causes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what is the progress in engaging corporations for philanthropic causes?

sections.label: Helping charities with technology expertise
sections.summary: The Government should reach out to charities and help them with technology expertise.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government should look into reaching out to these charities and helping them with the technology expertise.

sections.label: Many helping hands schemes complexity
sections.summary: VWOs, grassroots, religious entities, charitable organisations and volunteer groups introduced help schemes, but the wide range can be too complex for low-income and vulnerable beneficiaries to navigate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Driven by passion and in response to the call for "Many Helping Hands", various VWOs, grassroots, religious entities, charitable organisations or foundations and even informal volunteer groups have also introduced their own help schemes and programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: This is encouraging, but the wide range of schemes and programmes can be too complex for the low-income and vulnerable to grasp and navigate, and they are the very intended beneficiaries of these well-meaning initiatives.

sections.label: MSF ensuring low-income benefit
sections.summary: It asks how MSF will ensure low-income and vulnerable Singaporeans can fully benefit from these schemes and programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: How will MSF thus ensure that low-income and vulnerable Singaporeans will be able to fully benefit from these schemes and programmes?

sections.label: Improving social assistance delivery
sections.summary: It asks how MSF can further improve delivery of social assistance so the less fortunate receive holistic help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How can MSF further improve the delivery of social assistance so that the less fortunate can receive the holistic help they need?

sections.label: SSO achievements and outreach KPIs
sections.summary: It asks what SSO has achieved since inception, how many households it helped, and whether a KPI measures its outreach and effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What kind of achievements has been attained by SSO since its inception in helping families in need?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How many households has SSO helped thus far?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Is there a key performance indicator (KPI) to measure its outreach and effectiveness?

sections.label: Register for urgent cases data
sections.summary: It requests MSF prioritise assisting the most urgent cases quickly by having a register with data about them, by finding root causes and long-term solutions with families.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: By looking for the root causes of their predicament and working out the long-term solutions with the families, may I request MSF to prioritise assisting the most urgent cases quickly by having a register with data about them?

sections.label: Public rental housing hospital admissions
sections.summary: An SGH study of 16,000 patient histories found public rental housing patients had a 30% higher risk of frequent hospital admission.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Singapore Medical Journal recently published a study by Singapore General Hospital (SGH) doctors who looked back at 16,000 patient histories.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: They found that, in Singapore, patients staying in public rental housing had a 30% higher risk of being frequently admitted to hospital, even after adjusting for demographics and clinical conditions.

sections.label: Clementi flats and wheelchair ramps
sections.summary: Some older Clementi blocks cannot fit traditional HDB EASE wheelchair ramps, making it harder for seniors with mobility needs to go out.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In Clementi, some older blocks have flats which cannot accommodate the wheelchair ramp designs with the traditional Housing and Development Board's (HDB's) Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This means seniors with mobility needs find it harder to go out, see their doctor or participate in the community.

sections.label: Pioneer Generation Office renamed Silver Generation
sections.summary: Pioneer Generation Office will be renamed Silver Generation Office, reach seniors aged 65 and above, and be housed in AIC.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: Pioneer Generation Office (PGO) will be renamed Silver Generation Office (SGO) and reach out to new cohorts of seniors aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: SGO will be housed in the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC).

sections.label: SG Cares register of disadvantaged
sections.summary: A question asks whether MSF will facilitate a register of disadvantaged families, vulnerable children and needy adults on SG Cares.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: On SG Cares, will MSF facilitate having a register of the disadvantaged families, vulnerable children and needy adults?

sections.label: Follow-up and data sharing for assistance
sections.summary: It would be good to follow up assisted cases and for MSF to share data with other Ministries for cross-referrals and coordination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: It will be good to have follow-up on cases which are assisted to ensure continuity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: It will also be good for MSF to allow sharing of this data with other Ministries for cross-referrals and coordination in providing assistance.

sections.label: Wheels@Ubin wheelchair events
sections.summary: The first Wheels@Ubin event, held with SG50, brought 100 wheelchair users; the second concluded on 2 March with 120 participants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The first Wheels@Ubin event was held in conjunction with SG50, bringing 100 wheelchair users to the island.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The second edition of the event was successfully concluded on 2 March this year, with 120 participants.

sections.label: SG Cares volunteering opportunities
sections.summary: Since SG Cares launched in 2016, volunteering opportunities were curated and VWOs were helped to empower volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Since the launch of SG Cares in 2016, we have curated volunteering opportunities and worked with VWOs to improve their capabilities to empower volunteers.

sections.label: Next phase of SG Cares
sections.summary: The next phase of SG Cares aims to make greater collective impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In the next phase of SG Cares, we want to make greater collective impact.

sections.label: MSF, MOH, MCCY roles
sections.summary: MSF will improve assistance to vulnerable individuals and families, MOH will build support for seniors, and MCCY is growing the volunteering ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MSF, through more integrated delivery of social services and building up the social service sector, will improve the way we provide assistance to vulnerable individuals and families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MOH will take on the mandate of building a stronger system of support for our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) is growing our volunteering ecosystem, encouraging and enabling all of us to join in the national movement.

sections.label: Disability schemes at SSOs
sections.summary: From the third quarter of this year, clients can access disability schemes and services through SSOs, including SNTC and SG Enable offerings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: From the third quarter of this year, clients will be able to access schemes and services for persons with disabilities through our SSOs, such as those offered by the Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) and SG Enable.

sections.label: Bursaries and childcare support
sections.summary: From the second half of this year, ITE students from ComCare households will be assessed for bursaries without separate applications, and later support for childcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: From the second half of this year, the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) students from households receiving ComCare assistance will also be assessed for their eligibility to receive a Community Development Council (CDC)/Citizens Consultative Committee (CCC) Bursary or a Ministry of Education (MOE) Bursary, without having to apply separately for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Similarly, later this year, we will make it easier for mothers or single parents who are working or seeking work and receiving ComCare assistance to access financial support for childcare.

sections.label: Co-locating services with SSOs
sections.summary: Complementary services such as family services, employment assistance and SGO may be co-located with SSOs for client convenience and agency collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To bring about greater convenience to ComCare clients who need access to different services and facilitate collaboration across agencies, we will explore co-locating complementary services, such as family services, employment assistance and SGO, with our SSOs, to look at it from a client-centric point of view, instead of asking the client to travel from one point of the island to the other.

sections.label: SSO Geylang Serai video-conferencing pilot
sections.summary: The SSO at Geylang Serai will pilot video-conferencing links with SG Enable, SNTC and HDB from the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The SSO at Geylang Serai, for example, will pilot video-conferencing links with SG Enable, SNTC and HDB from the end of this year.

sections.label: MSF building up SSOs and networks
sections.summary: MSF will continue building up SSOs and social service networks, which will take time and support from VWOs, agencies, volunteers, corporations and society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: I have also explained how MSF will continue to build up the SSOs and the social service networks on the ground to collectively direct our motivations and resources to make an even greater impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This will, of course, take time and the support of VWOs, agencies, volunteers, corporations and all members of society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Ultimately, I hope all Singaporeans will recognise that the success of SG Cares rests upon an important truth, that is, we are all responsible for one another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: When we say that we are Singaporeans, we recognise the bond that ties us together as a community and society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We recognise our responsibilities and duties to one another, especially in times of need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Along the way, we have been helped by others, like our parents, friends, teachers and even complete strangers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We must recognise this and always pay it forward.

sections.label: ILTC subsidies and ElderShield review
sections.summary: ILTC subsidies were enhanced in 2012, ElderShield is being reviewed with recommendations by mid-year, and $2 billion is set aside for ElderShield subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In 2012, intermediate and long-term care (ILTC) subsidies were enhanced to cover up to two-thirds of Singaporean households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As many Members know, we are reviewing ElderShield to provide stronger support for disability in old age, and recommendations of the review committee will be released by mid-year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This year’s Budget has put aside $2 billion for ElderShield subsidies to ensure premiums will be affordable.

sections.label: PG Ambassadors community of care
sections.summary: PG Ambassadors have connected with more than 400,000 seniors in almost 800,000 engagements since 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Our PG Ambassadors remain the cornerstone of our efforts to create local communities of care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: They have connected with more than 400,000 seniors in almost 800,000 engagements since 2014.

sections.label: HPB volunteer Health Ambassadors
sections.summary: The 15,000 volunteer Health Ambassadors and Health Advocates from HPB come from all walks of life and play an important role in health promotion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The 15,000 volunteer Health Ambassadors and Health Advocates from our Health Promotion Board (HPB) come from all walks of life and play an important role in health promotion and raising public awareness.

sections.label: Respite options for caregivers
sections.summary: Respite options include 10 senior care centres, over 40 nursing homes for up to a month, and the Eldersit programme for seniors with dementia at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Providing respite options will give relief to caregivers who need help for a few hours over the weekend.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: They can leave their loved ones at one of the 10 senior care centres across Singapore, where they will be looked after.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: For those who need a longer respite, they can have their elderly cared for at one of the over 40 nursing homes for several days, up to a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In addition, our Eldersit programme provides an eldersitter, just like babysitter, to look after seniors with dementia at their homes.

sections.label: Corporate giving programme and Fullerton Academy
sections.summary: Close to 1,000 companies joined a five-month corporate giving programme, and one launched the Fullerton Academy to train youths for employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Since its inception, close to 1,000 companies have come on board.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In this five-month programme, corporate giving advocates across companies come together to share good practices and develop proposals for more impactful corporate giving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Putting its proposal into action, it launched the Fullerton Academy last month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The Academy mobilises hotel staff and partners as volunteers to provide training for youths from REACH Community Services in areas, such as culinary, etiquette and creative arts, that will help prepare them for future employment.

sections.label: Micro-volunteerism trend in Singapore
sections.summary: Community needs can be made bite-sized and flexible, and micro-volunteerism is an increasing trend allowing busy Singaporeans to slot doing good into their schedules.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Community needs can be made bite-sized and flexible, so that more Singaporeans can get involved whatever their skills, interests and commitments in their current life stage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We are seeing an increasing trend of micro-volunteerism in Singapore – volunteerism broken into discrete tasks with flexible commitments, allowing on-the-go Singaporeans to slot doing good into their busy schedules.

sections.label: Familiarity with online giving
sections.summary: About 50% of Singaporeans are familiar with online giving, and 25% actively support charitable social media campaigns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Today, about 50% of Singaporeans are already familiar with online giving, and 25% actively support charitable social media campaigns.

sections.label: Pilots in Bedok and Jurong East
sections.summary: Pilots in Bedok and Jurong East bring partners together to co-develop coordination models that can be replicated in other towns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: To do this, we have set up pilots in Bedok and Jurong East to bring partners together to co-develop coordination models that can be replicated in other towns.

sections.label: Partners providing senior care services
sections.summary: St Luke's ElderCare provides rehabilitation, Touch Community Services ensures home visits and counselling, and Thye Hua Kwan offers recreational activities and courses for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Partners, such as St Luke's ElderCare, provides rehabilitation programmes; Touch Community Services ensures regular home visits and provides services, such as counselling and transitional care from the hospital; and Thye Hua Kwan offers recreational activities and courses to keep the senior engaged and connected with the community.

sections.label: MCCY volunteer mobilisation and SG Cares
sections.summary: MCCY mobilises volunteers through arts, heritage, youth and sport initiatives, and SG Cares seeks to build a civic culture of care, consideration and contribution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: MCCY has been working to mobilise volunteers through the arts, heritage, youth and sport through initiatives, such as Team Nila, SportCares, HeritageCares and the Youth Corps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Through SG Cares, we seek to build a civic culture of care, consideration and contribution where all Singaporeans can work together for a better Singapore.

sections.label: IPS survey on social division
sections.summary: An IPS survey found social division in Singapore may now be based on class rather than race or religion, requiring whole-of-Government effort.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in a recent survey done on Social Capital in Singapore by the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS), it found that social division in Singapore may now be based on class rather than race or religion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: While it may not be realistic to expect that all our children and individuals will have access to similar learning opportunities to develop their talent and that everyone would have the same access to job and career opportunities, as a society, we must still aspire to do so, and our systems and structures must continue to strive to provide opportunities for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: To do this, it will require deliberate and a whole-of-Government effort to mitigate inequality of opportunity, ensure social mobility and foster social integration.

sections.label: IPS survey on class boundaries
sections.summary: Concerns were raised after an IPS survey released last December found class boundaries more salient than gender, racial and religious boundaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Concerns were raised following a nationwide survey conducted by IPS released last December which found that class boundaries tend to be more salient than gender, racial and religious boundaries.

sections.label: CYPA age cut-off question
sections.summary: The CYPA protects youths only up to 16, and a question asks whether the Government will raise the cut-off age to 18.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our Children and Young Persons Act (CYPA) currently only protects youths up to the age of 16.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This means that youths between 16 and 18 do not enjoy the Act’s protections, such as not having their particulars published in the media and having more sentencing options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In February 2017, an interagency committee chaired by the Attorney-General's Chambers submitted a number of recommendations to the Government, including the recommendation to raise the CYPA cut-off age from 16 to 18.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One year on, has the Government come to any conclusions on doing so, and when will this be effected?

sections.label: Children and Young Persons Act protection
sections.summary: Under the CYPA, a child in need of care or protection may be removed from a parent and placed in care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The principal legal tool used to intervene when a child or young person is neglected by his or her parent is the Children and Young Persons Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under the Act, a child or young person is deemed to be in need of care or protection if his or her situation falls within the nine enumerated categories stated therein.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In such an event, the Director of Social Welfare, a protector or a Police Officer is empowered to remove the child from the custody of the parent and place him or her in a place of care and protection.

sections.label: Compulsory Education Act violations
sections.summary: In 2003, the House was informed there were about 10 cases of violations under the Compulsory Education Act per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In 2003, this House was informed that there were about 10 cases of violations under the Compulsory Education Act per year.

sections.label: Singaporeans aged 65 and above
sections.summary: By then, one in four Singaporeans, or 900,000, will be aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: By then, one in four Singaporeans, or 900,000 of us, will be aged 65 and above.

sections.label: MOH budget growth question
sections.summary: Asks whether MOH's budget will one day outstrip MOE or MINDEF, placing greater demands on MSF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Stating it starkly, will we one day see MOH's budget outstrip that of MOE or even the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) and thereby placing even greater demands on MSF as well?

sections.label: Survey on generational support views
sections.summary: About 40% felt Government should support, while 41% believed each generation should care for itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: About 40% felt that the Government should chime in on the support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Interestingly, 41% believed each generation should take care of itself, without support from other generations.

sections.label: Longer LPA registration waits
sections.summary: OPG told applicants LPA reviews would exceed the preferred 15 to 20 working days due to high application volume.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: To illustrate, OPG has, in recent months, written to applicants to register LPAs that it would take longer than the preferred 15 to 20 working days to review their applications due to a greater than expected volume of LPA applications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I know of one case where an LPA sent to OPG for registration is still pending after three months.

sections.label: Revoked LPA count
sections.summary: As at 28 February 2018, the number of Revoked LPAs was recorded as 1,841.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: As at 28 February 2018, the number of Revoked LPAs was recorded as 1,841.

sections.label: CPF top-ups for caregivers
sections.summary: Asks whether Government would consider CPF top-ups for full-time informal caregivers in low-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider measures, such as Central Provident Fund (CPF) top-ups for full-time informal caregivers in low-income households to reduce the pressure of being underemployed and under-prepared for retirement, as a result of taking on the responsibilities of caring for their loved seniors?

sections.label: Childcare subsidy and fee rise
sections.summary: Singapore Citizen children get up to $300 monthly childcare subsidy; since 2011 median fees rose 22%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Currently, Singapore Citizen children are eligible for a basic subsidy of up to $300 for childcare per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Since 2011, the childcare operators have raised the median fees by 22%.

sections.label: Student care subsidy enhancement
sections.summary: Student care subsidy was enhanced from 1 January 2016 for families with monthly household income at the 20th percentile and below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Subsidy for student care was enhanced since 1 January 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This subsidy is made available to families with a monthly household income of 20th percentile and below.

sections.label: My First Skool fee hikes
sections.summary: My First Skool raised childcare fees by $6 to $33 and infant care fees by $5 to $20 this year, after hikes in 2013, 2015 and 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, parents who send their children to anchor operator My First Skool were hit by news of another school fee hike this year of between $6 and $33 for childcare; and $5 and $20 for infant care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These hikes this year come hot on the heels of similar hikes by My First Skool in 2013, 2015 and 2016 which, cumulatively, mean that it now costs $100 a month or more, and more than $1,200 a year to enroll a child into My First Skool.

sections.label: Fee cap as price shield
sections.summary: Four fee hikes since 2013 suggest the fee cap can act as a shield to raise prices when parents lack clear reasons for hikes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Even though the absolute increase is below the fee cap established by the Ministry, four fee hikes since 2013 appear to suggest that the fee cap can operate as a shield to raise prices, particularly when parents do not have a clear idea for the reasons behind the price hikes.

sections.label: Cost pressures on anchor operators
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry can share details on cost pressures impacting anchor operators in child and infant care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share details on the cost pressures impacting anchor operators in the child and infant care space?

sections.label: Malay Language Month chairperson role
sections.summary: The speaker states he is Chairperson of Malay Language Month, an annual event celebrating and encouraging public use of Malay.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: (In Malay):   I am the Chairperson of the Malay Language Month this year which is an annual event to celebrate and encourage the use of Malay Language amongst the public.

sections.label: Preschool mother tongue teaching materials
sections.summary: Preschool educators told the speaker they have difficulty getting suitable teaching materials, and he asks what the Ministry can do.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: In my discussions with preschool educators in my role as the Malay Language Month Chairperson, some of them said they have difficulties in getting suitable teaching materials for their students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I understand that improvements have been made in this matter whereby materials like Big Books were made available for teachers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As Singapore prioritises bilingual education, what can the Ministry do to ensure that preschool students receive quality mother tongue education?

sections.label: Enabling Masterplans and UN Convention
sections.summary: Singapore has had three Enabling Masterplans and ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2013, with the latest plan at implementation stage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Since 2007, Singapore has seen three Enabling Masterplans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Singapore has also ratified the United Nations (UN) Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2013, signalling the Government's serious commitment to the disability community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The latest Enabling Masterplan which will see us through 2021 is at its implementation stage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There is also a need to watch tightly the implementation of a plan that involves the whole of society, report to society, and systematically and visibly invite and engage society to form part of the often complex solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I therefore seek an update from the Minister on the progress of the latest Enabling Masterplan.

sections.label: Early childhood investment and preschool places
sections.summary: Investment in the early childhood sector will double over five years, adding 40,000 preschool places mainly in estates with young families.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Research has shown that the early experiences of children provide the foundation for their future learning, behaviour and health.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Thus, we will double our investment in the early childhood sector over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will introduce 40,000 more preschool places, mainly in estates with young families.

sections.label: Anchor Operator preschools and MTL teachers
sections.summary: Preschools run by five Anchor Operators providing Malay or Tamil will double to 350 by 2022, possibly needing over 1,000 more MTL teachers by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The number of preschools run by five Anchor Operators (AOPs) providing Malay or Tamil, will double to 350 by 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To support the sector’s growth, we may need over 1,000 more MTL teachers by 2020.

sections.label: MSF 2016 family survey results
sections.summary: In a 2016 MSF survey, 93% of respondents agreed they had a close-knit family and 98% agreed it was their responsibility to care for their parents.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In a survey conducted by MSF in 2016, 93% of respondents agreed they had a close-knit family, and 98% agreed it was their responsibility to take care of their parents, regardless of their qualities or faults.

sections.label: Preschool places and early experiences
sections.summary: As noted by Ms Jessica Tan, early experiences are the foundation for future learning, behaviour and health, so 40,000 more preschool places will be introduced over five years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As noted by Ms Jessica Tan, the early experiences of children are also the foundation for their future learning, behaviour and health.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Thus, we will introduce 40,000 more preschool places over the next five years, mainly in estates with young families.

sections.label: Fee-capped preschool places by 2023
sections.summary: By 2023, two in three preschoolers will have a place in preschools where fees are capped.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: By 2023, two in three preschoolers will have a place in such preschools, where the fees are capped.

sections.label: Early Childhood Industry Transformation Map
sections.summary: ECDA worked with operators, unions and industry associations to develop manpower strategies in the Early Childhood Industry Transformation Map, released today.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: To ensure sustainable growth, ECDA has worked with operators, unions and industry associations to develop innovative and forward-looking manpower strategies in the Early Childhood Industry Transformation Map (ITM) which we are releasing today.

sections.label: 1,000 senior professional positions
sections.summary: Over the next five years, some 1,000 senior professional positions will be created, doubling the current number.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Over the next five years, they will create some 1,000 senior professional positions, doubling the current number.

sections.label: AOP preschools and MTL teachers
sections.summary: By 2022, AOP preschools providing Malay or Tamil are planned to double to 350, and over 1,000 more MTL teachers may be needed by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: By 2022, we plan for the number of AOP preschools providing Malay or Tamil to double to 350.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: To support the sector's growth, we may need over 1,000 more MTL teachers by 2020.

sections.label: LPA applications tripled
sections.summary: LPA applications tripled from 4,600 in 2014 to 13,900 in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Since then, the number of LPA applications has tripled from 4,600 in 2014 to 13,900 in 2017.

sections.label: Reasons for LPA revocations
sections.summary: About 80% of revocations were due to death of the donor or donee, and 15% were revoked upon the donor's decision.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: To date, about 80% of revocations were due to death of the donor or donee, and a further 15% were revoked upon the donor’s decision.

sections.label: Public sector hiring persons with disabilities
sections.summary: The public sector hired over 70 new employees with disabilities in two years, and the Special Employment Credit now supports up to 80% of travel costs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The public sector has been leading the way and hired over 70 new employees with disabilities in the past two years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Over the past two years, 2,700 new employees and over 1,300 new employers have benefited from the Special Employment Credit which supports employers in hiring employees with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The scheme now supports up to 80% of the cost of travel, up from 50% previously, and has been extended to private hire cars.

sections.label: SNTC caregiver outreach
sections.summary: Over five years, SNTC will work with community partners including SSOs to reach over 1,700 caregivers of persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Over the next five years, SNTC will work with community partners, including the SSOs, to reach out to more than 1,700 caregivers of persons with disabilities.

sections.label: CAF assessment access points
sections.summary: From 1 April 2018, persons with disabilities and caregivers can get CAF assessment at special education schools or disability care services, or be linked to Therapy Hubs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: From 1 April 2018, persons with disabilities and their caregivers can approach the special education schools or disability care services, such as Day Activity Centres, to have the assessment done onsite or be linked up to the Therapy Hubs for the CAF assessment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We estimate that about 1,000 persons with disabilities and their caregivers could benefit from this.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As my Minister has announced, we are working towards making information and referral to services by SG Enable and SNTC available at our SSOs through video conferencing.

sections.label: KidSTART pilot for low-income children
sections.summary: The KidSTART pilot began in 2016 to identify children from low-income families early and support them through health, learning and developmental support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For children from low-income families, we embarked on the KidSTART pilot in 2016 to proactively identify them early and support them intensively, through early access to health, learning and developmental support.

sections.label: SSOs and ComCare enhancements
sections.summary: Since 2013 SSOs were progressively set up, and ComCare coverage was enhanced by expanding income criteria and increasing Long-Term Assistance cash amounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Since 2013, we have progressively set up SSOs to bring more accessible and coordinated social assistance to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In the past few years, we have enhanced the coverage of ComCare assistance by expanding the income criteria and increased the cash amount of Long-Term Assistance.

sections.label: Interagency committee on offending
sections.summary: An interagency committee of Government agencies and VWOs will be set up to tackle offending and re-offending and support offenders' rehabilitation and reintegration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For example, we will set up an interagency committee, comprising Government agencies and VWOs, to see how we can all work much closer together to tackle offending, re-offending, and to support offenders to rehabilitate and reintegrate into the community.

sections.label: 24 SSOs island-wide
sections.summary: Since 2013, a total of 24 SSOs have been set up island-wide so Singaporeans in need can access assistance more easily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Since 2013, we have set up a total of 24 SSOs island-wide so that Singaporeans in need can have easier access to assistance.

sections.label: CYPA age review update
sections.summary: Ms Sylvia Lim asked whether the age in CYPA will be raised to 18, and the youth justice system review is ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked for an update on whether we will be raising the age in CYPA to 18 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Our review of the youth justice system is ongoing, with CYPA being one component.

sections.label: Social workers at Police divisions
sections.summary: Since 2016, social workers have been stationed at Police divisions to assess youth offenders up to 19 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Since 2016, we have stationed social workers at Police divisions to assess the risks and needs of youth offenders up to 19 years of age.

sections.label: MSF homelessness case numbers
sections.summary: MSF assists around 300 reported homelessness cases each year, a figure that has remained thereabouts for five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MSF assists around 300 reported cases of homelessness each year, and this figure has remained thereabouts for the past five years.

sections.label: Welfare Homes and Transitional Shelters
sections.summary: Those unable to work with no means or family support may enter Welfare Homes, and those with no housing options may get Transitional Shelters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Individuals who are unable to work and have no financial means and family support may be admitted to Welfare Homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Individuals who have exhausted all housing options may be supported by Transitional Shelters which provide temporary accommodation.

sections.label: Social Service Sector Strategic Thrusts
sections.summary: In 2016, NCSS and social service partners set out a vision and roadmap for the sector through the 4ST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In 2016, NCSS and our social service partners laid out a vision and roadmap for the sector through the Social Service Sector Strategic Thrusts (4ST).

sections.label: Salary norms and MSF funding
sections.summary: After this year's review, salary norms will rise by up to 12%, raising MSF recurrent funding to VWO-run programmes by about $11 million in FY2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: After this year's review, the salary norms will increase by up to 12% across the various funded social service professions and job levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Accordingly, MSF’s recurrent funding to our VWO-run programmes will increase by about $11 million, or 5%, in financial year (FY) 2018.

sections.label: New Work-Learn Programme partners
sections.summary: SSG, SUSS and Nanyang Polytechnic will introduce a new Work-Learn Programme in the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Earlier, Minister Ong Ye Kung had shared that SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG), the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) and Nanyang Polytechnic will be introducing a new Work-Learn Programme (WLP) in the second half of this year.

sections.label: Skills Framework for Social Service
sections.summary: Social service professionals need requisite skillsets, and a Skills Framework for Social Service will launch later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Social service professionals need to be equipped with the requisite skillsets to be effective and to be prepared for future demands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will be launching the Skills Framework for Social Service later this year.

sections.label: SHARE As One matching grant
sections.summary: Under SHARE As One, the Government provides dollar-for-dollar matching for new and incremental donations above 2015's level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Under SHARE As One, the Government provides dollar-for-dollar matching for new and incremental donations to the SHARE programme above 2015’s level.

sections.label: SHARE As One extension and opt-out
sections.summary: SHARE as One brought about a million dollars more in 2016, its matching grant extends from 2018 to 2021, and ComChest is implementing an opt-out system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: SHARE as One has successfully brought in about a million dollars more in new and incremental donations in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As announced by the Minister for Finance, the matching grant for SHARE as One will be extended from 2018 till 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: ComChest is working to implement an opt-out contribution system for SHARE in the public sector.

sections.label: Elderly residents with refused family help
sections.summary: Some elderly residents said their children refused to help yet they have immediate needs, and MSF was asked how it will balance and assure them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Some elderly residents have shared that their children simply refused to help and yet they have immediate needs to be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: How will MSF achieve the balance and help assure those in need that they will not be left in the cold?

sections.label: Addressing elderly needs and family reconciliation
sections.summary: Immediate needs like health, financial difficulty and welfare are addressed first, then FSCs and social workers work to bring family reconciliation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: When an elderly person who might technically have family support runs into difficulties, we need to first address immediately needs like health, financial difficulty that needs to be addressed immediately and their welfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Beyond that, our FSCs, counsellors, social workers from the FSCs, including those from specialist agencies, if need be, will come in and work alongside us to see how we can bring reconciliation within the family and encourage the family to step up and to play their part.

sections.label: MTL teacher training and support
sections.summary: Plans, training programmes, scholarships and training awards are being provided for MTL teachers, with WSG facilitating and Work Trial programmes relevant to them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Yes, indeed, we have plans and also training programmes for the MTL teachers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: There are scholarships as well as training awards to be given.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: WSG will also look at it to see how we can facilitate the process.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Some of the programmes that are being rolled out, such as Work Trial and the Enhanced Work Trial, will also be relevant to our MTL teachers.

sections.label: SSOs identifying complex case leads
sections.summary: Through SSOs, the identification of proper case leads for complex cases will continue to be overseen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Second, through our SSOs, we will continue to oversee the identification of proper case leads for complex cases.

sections.label: Early identification and family support
sections.summary: MSF and ECDA, with KKH, run a pilot to identify and support families so children get a better start in life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On the Member's second point about whether we can identify people from a young age and make sure that they are supported as far as possible, through as much of life as possible, that really is what Mr Speaker initiated when he started KidSTART because he dreamt about the possibility of making sure that these children can aspire and dream and be able to meet those dreams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MSF and ECDA, partnering some hospitals, in this case KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital (KKH), and a pilot to identify, but not stigmatise, to be able to approach and not force, to be able to encourage and not cajole these families to come on board to show that the children will have a better start in life if they, number one, enroll their children in early childhood, ensure that the childcare centres or kindergartens are adequately resourced to support them, to work with the families, including the parents, to give them the skills they need to contribute more effectively as parents, especially when one or both of them are working, or is a single parent family and be able to rope in and pull in the schemes from across the landscape of the Government and the community try to help these families and enable them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: How far this goes through the child's journey and through teenage and adulthood, we will see as this pilot develops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But early indications show that it is welcomed by the families, both the information and the support and awareness, and welcomed by the childcare centres who get the support they need to enable these children to bloom.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: One, still continuing on the SSO issue, I have worked with very good SSOs before, but now that the landscape is going to be more SSO-centric, how do we ensure that they have the muscle and the influence and even properly resourced to be able to coordinate all the various many helping hands together?

sections.label: Enabling Masterplan key thrusts
sections.summary: The latest Enabling Masterplan has four key thrusts, nine strategic directions and 20 recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Based on the Senior Parliamentary Secretary's update, things are really all in order but the latest Enabling Masterplan has four key thrusts, nine strategic directions and 20 recommendations.

sections.label: Respite, preschool and sheltered enterprises
sections.summary: Three matters are raised: a respite pilot ending, a deaf community preschool model, and sheltered enterprises for the more severely disabled.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: One is the respite programme that is about to be terminated because it is a pilot.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: The second one is what the deaf community has asked for − a preschool model that is something like the one at Mayflower that MOE has started.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: And the third one is on sheltered enterprises, not just social enterprises, which are really quite important for those who are more severely disabled but can do some light duty work instead of sending them to day activity centres.

sections.label: IMDA PlayMaker technology-enabled toys
sections.summary: IMDA has rolled out the PlayMaker programme introducing technology-enabled toys as a learning process for kids, which will continue.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As such, IMDA has rolled out a PlayMaker programme.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: It is part of the process to introduce technology-enabled toys as a learning process for the kids.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: A few of the schools, for example, Skool4Kidz have also looked at it and have implemented it.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: What we will do is that we will continue this process because we also believe and share the Member's view that it is something that we should prepare our kids for and immerse them, and make it natural because that is the space where they are going to grow up in and that is where they can play a bigger part in the future.

sections.label: Preschool smart solutions adoption
sections.summary: About 800 preschools indicated interest in smart solutions, with half implementing them and savings of 40-100 man-hours monthly, while over 50 schools using centralised meal catering cut costs by up to 10%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Today, about 800 preschools have already indicated their interest to adopt smart solutions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, about half of these centres have implemented some of these solutions and they can expect a savings of 40-100 man-hours a month.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: When we also look at the centralised meal catering services, more than 50 schools have taken up this arrangement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: And we found that it has reduced costs by as much as 10%.
